messages:
Emma: FYI ap-northeast-1 private keystore IAM tighten is triggering a NATGW conntrack spike. GPU warm pool nodes are failing keystore handshakes and audit logs are spiking. Anyone watching?
Raj: Saw the alerts, paging now. Warm pool prewarm failures line up with lots of keystore auth retries.
Luis: That policy change was merged yesterday evening. TF snippet from the change: ```json
{
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Action": ["sts:AssumeRole"],
      "Condition": {
        "StringNotEquals": { "aws:SourceVpce": "vpce-0f1a2b3c4d" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
Luis: The Deny narrowed the service-role handoff path, causing the keystore agent to fall back to more aggressive IAM calls from nodes. That created a large number of short-lived connections and flooded NAT conntrack.
oncall-sre: Conntrack snapshot: ```
entries: 945123
max: 1000000
TCP: 175430 active connections
```
oncall-sre: Warm pool status: 16/30 ready. 14 nodes hung at "keystore: handshake" step.
Emma: Two options: revert the policy (fast) or add an allowlist for the keystore VPC endpoint so the keystore service still authenticates via the intended path. Revert is lowest friction.
Raj: Short-term we can bump conntrack max to 2M on NAT hosts (sysctl) to buy time. Command: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000`. We'll need a rolling restart or apply via cloud-init. This is a bandaid though.
Luis: I'll open an urgent revert PR to tf to restore previous policy scope and tag it urgent/keystore. Also prepare a minimal patch that adds `aws:SourceVpce` allowlist for the keystore endpoint.
Emma: oncall approves revert, proceed. :thumbsup:
DeployBot: Started terraform apply by Luis (run: apply-2026-04-03-21:07).
DeployBot: Terraform apply finished 00: 1 resource updated (aws_iam_policy_document keystore-policy). run_id=apply-2026-04-03-21:07
oncall-sre: Conntrack entries dropping now: 940k -> 260k in 6m, warm pool coming back up.
Emma: Warm pool at 25/30 ready, keystore handshake failures decreasing.
Raj: Follow-ups: 1) Revert temporary allowlist after we validate long-term fix, 2) Implement retry rate-limiting in the keystore client, 3) Add a runbook entry for IAM tightening impact on NAT conntrack and alerts.
Luis: Taking ownership of the TF revert, keystore patch, and filing INFRA-4932 with steps and rollback instructions.
Emma: Monitoring for two hours. If conntrack > 80% again, escalate to network oncall. Thanks everyone.
